body: Why Log W-13. Kentrou et al. 2024, eClinicalMedicine (PMC11001629): n=1,211 Dutch autistic adults; 24.6% perceived misdiagnosis (women 31.7%, men 16.7%); equal by gender within those with any prior diagnosis. Supporting: Au-Yeung et al., Autism (online 2018). Fair side: perceived, not confirmed; self-selected, highly educated Dutch sample. Type: reader-dependent criterion.
evidence: Published, peer-reviewed: Kentrou et al. 2024, eClinicalMedicine (PMC11001629)
plain: One in four autistic adults, and one in three autistic women, report a psychiatric diagnosis before autism that they now judge wrong. Women get more earlier diagnoses; the rate per diagnosis is equal.
